trust_decision.summary: FailureApp#redirect_url decides the post-timeout redirect target; on non-GET requests it trusts the raw Referer header (full URL, any host/scheme) and passes it to redirect_to.

landing_point.why: The summary names Timeoutable + request.referrer; the only request.referrer read in lib/app is this line in the timeout branch of redirect_url.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any authenticated non-GET HTTP request whose session has timed out (Warden throw at lib/devise/hooks/timeoutable.rb:28 -> FailureApp.call -> respond -> redirect -> redirect_url)
Public controller helper store_location_for (lib/devise/controllers/store_location.rb:36) and, after the fix, FailureApp#redirect_url via the shared private extract_path_from_location
fix_sites.module_kind: shared controller mixin (helper), nil-guard for opaque URIs (javascript:, mailto:) whose uri.path is nil and would otherwise raise in remove_domain_from_uri at lib/devise/controllers/store_location.rb:68

O3_reason_to_dismiss: store_location_for is a separate login-return feature already stripping domains; a solver can argue opaque-URI handling there is unrelated robustness, not the timeout redirect, and write a local referer check in failure_app instead.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After a non-GET timeout the user must still be redirected back to the same-site page they came from (full same-host Referer URL), and fall back to the sign-in URL when there is no usable referer; rejecting all referers or all absolute URLs breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: absolute external URL in Referer (http://evil.example/phishing) -> reduced to path '/phishing' (fix.diff:85-88)
opaque URI with no path (javascript:alert(1), mailto:) -> nil -> sign-in fallback (fix.diff:26-27, fix.diff:91-98)
unparseable URI -> nil via parse_uri rescue (lib/devise/controllers/store_location.rb:45-49)
leading multiple slashes squeezed to one (protocol-relative) via remove_domain_from_uri (lib/devise/controllers/store_location.rb:68)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Timeout on GET: redirect_url returns raw attempted_path (from Warden options) to redirect_to without extract_path_from_location, unlike store_location! which sanitises the same value
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: attempted_path is the server-side request path, not attacker-supplied header data; the advisory only names the non-GET Referer branch
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fix site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a non-timeout failure path (e.g. a 'redirect back to referer' option for unauthenticated non-GET) that reads request.referrer directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: redirect already special-cases timeout flash; a maintainer extending 'return to previous page' to other warden messages would copy the referer branch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: OmniAuth failure redirect honouring an origin/return param or Referer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OmniAuth supplies omniauth.origin; returning the user to it on failure is a common customisation
'return to where you were after logout' is a frequent feature request and would sit in a different controller from the FailureApp

O9_family: open redirect (CWE-601) via untrusted redirect target

O10_build.project_tests: test/integration/timeoutable_test.rb, test/controllers/helpers_test.rb, test/failure_app_test.rb (sqlite in-memory test app)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare URI(request.referrer).host with request.host in failure_app.rb and fall back to scope_url otherwise (misses opaque/edge shapes or diverges from the published '/phishing' path-only behaviour)

out_of_scope_notes: FailureApp is ActionController::Metal, so Rails' raise_on_open_redirects (configured on ActionController::Base) likely does not guard its redirect_to; not pursued.
unverified: O8 GET-branch: whether attempted_path can start with '//' or carry a host depends on Warden (sets attempted_path outside this repo) and Rails router path normalisation; not checked.
Repo size not measured (no shell); Devise is a small library and likely trips tiny_repo (<5 MB), which lessons-v2 lists as never producing hard tasks.
Hidden-test ambiguity: published fix maps external referer to its path ('/phishing', fix.diff:88) rather than rejecting it; a correct alternative fix (fallback to sign-in) would fail that assertion.
Present-in-latest for O8 unknown (no latest release provided).
